items.title: How to check recruitment requirements item by item?

values: Materials and setup｜All data and plans are editorially fictional

You are organizing an after-school activity questionnaire for a fictional project, as a paper or local spreadsheet exercise only. All IDs and values are fictional; do not recruit, contact or record real participants, and do not conduct real research.

E1｜Exercise rules: the analysis includes only unique IDs flagged Y; for completely identical duplicate rows, keep the first row. The source table must be kept complete, and exclusions and changes are recorded in the log. Y／N is an exercise inclusion flag and does not replace real informed consent or ethics judgment.

E2｜Six source rows, with columns in order ID, inclusion flag, weekly activity hours, satisfaction: first 10｜Y｜2｜4; second 11｜Y｜3｜5; third 12｜Y｜99｜99; fourth 11｜Y｜3｜5; fifth 13｜N｜4｜3; sixth 14｜Y｜1｜blank. The fourth and the second are completely identical; no other rows exist.

E3｜Codebook: hours allow 0—40, and satisfaction allows 1—5. In both columns 99 means missing, and blanks are also missing; missing must not be treated as 0. Each mean uses only the rows with valid values for that variable as the denominator; ID 12 is still an included subject and must not be removed from the included count because both columns are missing.

E4｜Erroneous draft: “All six rows are valid participants, and both columns are calculated with n = 6. This study proves that the activity improved the well-being of the whole population.” The materials contain no sampling representativeness, random assignment, control or before-and-after comparison, and no well-being variable.

E5｜The assistant organizes according to the given exercise rules and flags issues, and the responsible person reviews methods, applicability and the manuscript; the plan, ethics and data access of real projects are confirmed by institutional rules, and assistants cannot approve or exempt on their own.
Tasks and outputs
Keep the E2 source table and write the codebook and line-by-line cleaning log according to E1—E3, listing analysis inclusion IDs and the valid n, sum and mean for each variable.

Correct E4 into a verifiable description, keep the research conditions that were not provided, and submit a one-page list for the responsible person to confirm; do not invent causal, representative or ethics conclusions.
Reference answers (finish independently first, then check)

The circled fourth duplicates the circled second, so the analysis copy keeps the circled second; the circled fifth is N and is not included in the analysis. The unique included IDs are 10, 11, 12 and 14, 4 in total. The original six rows are still kept, and the first, second, third and sixth enter the analysis copy; the two 99s of the third become missing, and the blank satisfaction of the sixth is missing.

Valid hours values are 2, 3 and 1, with n = 3, sum = 6 and mean = 2 hours/week. Valid satisfaction values are 4 and 5, with n = 2, sum = 9 and mean = 4.5/5. The included count 4, hours n3 and scores n2 are different definitions, and missing is not treated as 0.

This is only a description of the exercise data and cannot support conclusions about the whole population, improved well-being or causal effects.” The responsible person must verify the real plan, missing value rules, sampling and analysis interpretation; this exercise conducts no research.

description.text: Assist social science research teams in collecting, coding, cleaning and managing data, reviewing literature and producing statistical tables and draft research reports. The key is to make source materials, processing rules and analysis denominators traceable, and to hand research design, ethics and uncertainty in conclusions to the responsible person for review. A research assistant title grants no independent ethics approval or clinical diagnostic authority.
